chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Yaqub al-Hashimi, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Burayd — from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) — regarding His (God's) saying, Mighty and Majestic:
And We did not send before you any Rasool, or Prophet, or Muhaddith.

key_terms.رسول: Rasool — a messenger sent with a new divine scripture and shariah
key_terms.محدَّث: Muhaddith — one to whom angels speak with divine knowledge, without being a prophet; the Shia doctrine applies this to the Imams
key_terms.نبي: Nabi — a prophet who receives revelation but does not bring a new scripture

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a Rasool, a Prophet, and a Muhaddith in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imams al-Baqir and al-Sadiq (peace be upon them both) are cited regarding Quran 22:52, in a hadith that includes the word 'Muhaddith' (one to whom God speaks through angels without prophethood) in the verse — a reading that supports the Shia doctrine of Imamate. This hadith establishes a theological distinction between three categories: a Rasool (messenger who receives a new scripture), a Nabi (prophet who receives revelation without a new book), and a Muhaddith (one divinely spoken to, such as the Imams). The audience of early Shia scholars would have understood this as scriptural validation of the Imams' special status as recipients of divine communication.
word_analysis: Muhaddith (one spoken to by divine inspiration)

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Yaqoub Al Hashimy, from Marwan Bin Muslim, from Bureyd, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding His<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[22:52] And We did not Send any Rasool or Prophet, or a Muhaddith before you (Please note that the word ‘Muhaddith’ is missing from this Verse in the current version of the Quran).
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya have narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn Hassan from Faddal from Ali ibn Ya’qub al-Hashimi from Marwan ibn Muslim from Burayd who has said the following. “I asked abu Ja‘far (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, “Satan would try to tamper with the desires of every Prophet or Messenger or Muhaddith (Muhaddith is a commentary of Imam (a.s.), whom We sent . .’” [22:52].

I said, ““May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, the word Muhaddith does not exist in our reading. What then is the meaning of The Messenger, Prophet and Muhaddith?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “A messenger is one to whom the angel comes openly and speaks to him. A prophet is one who sees in his dream. Sometimes prophethood and messengership may exist in one person. Al-Muhaddith is one who hears the voice but does not see the person (of the angel).” I then asked, may Allah keep you well, “How would one know that what one sees in his dream is true and that it is from the angel?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “He receives help for success to know the angel. Allah has your book the last book and your Prophet the last of prophets.”
